name: Amazon Prime Air (blue, 737 freighters)
description: The narrowbody version of Amazon's scheme, on its 737-800 freighters: sky-blue fuselage with 'Prime Air' in big white letters behind the cockpit; a white band sweeps from the belly behind the wing up to the crown at the fin's root, and behind it the aft fuselage, tail cone and fin are dark slate; the white Amazon smile low across the fin; blue engines.

sources.title: Amazon Boeing 737-800 N7922A BWI MD1.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, Acroterion; the aircraft is N7933A)
sources.note: N7933A (Sun Country-flown 737-800BCF), left side, level, 2026-08-06: geometry, title, fin.

sources.note: EI-AZC (ASL Airlines Ireland) right side, 2026-03-18: the right side matches; the smile unmirrored; blue winglets and engines.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Amazon Air
sources.note: Fleet and contract operators (ATI, Atlas, Sun Country, Hawaiian, ASL Ireland, Cargojet, 21 Air, Quikjet); 'Prime Air' renamed Amazon Air in 2017 while the jets kept 'Prime Air' titles.

blue.name: sky blue (Prime blue on the 737s reads lighter than the 767 titles)

areas.name: white band from the belly behind the wing up to the crown at the fin root
dark slate aft fuselage and tail cone

logos.description: The Amazon smile: a curved white swoosh, thin at its left end, thickest under the middle, rising to the right into an arrowhead whose point is at its upper right (the corner of a short hook that drops down and back). Low across the fin, about four-fifths of its chord wide. Unmirrored on the right side (EI-AZC).

titles.style: 'Prime Air' in big white bold sans-serif, mixed case, italic (about 12°, Amazon's Prime wordmark), from just behind the forward door.

notes: Drawn on the 737-800 from N7933A (Sun Country, 2026-08-06, left) and EI-AZC (ASL Ireland, 2026-03-18, right); every Amazon 737 photographed (N5147A, N5153A, N5233A, N5693A, N7901A, EI-AZA...EI-AZG, VT-AAZ) wears it. A small 'Operated by <contractor>' line by the cockpit changes with the operator (Sun Country, ASL Airlines, Atlas; ASL's jets add 'Always High AIR'): left out. The white band is a little wider low down than on the 767's blue band; the belly under it isn't seen and is assumed to wrap. Winglets blue with a white root sweep (low). See ATN/prime-air for the 767 version. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on the 737-800 (B738 measured shape; N7933A left 2026-08-06, fitted with photo_trace and its doors; EI-AZC right 2026-04-09): the white band's edges re-measured off the fitted photo (straight diagonals as seen from the side, bending only near the crown) (its aft edge had been up to ~0.5 m too far forward low down); the title (italic, as on the 767s) runs ~0.14-0.42 with its cap top at y ~0.56 (it had been drawn ~30% too tall); EI-AZC's right-side title sits ~0.5 m further aft and a little higher than N7933A's left one, so operators' paint shops differ slightly. The white band continues up the aft edge of the blue dorsal fillet to the fin's leading edge: not drawn (the fillet takes the fin's root paint).
history: New in Open Liveries (2026-11-13). The blue narrowbody version came with Amazon's first 737-800BCFs in 2019 (N855DM shown at the 2019 Paris Air Show).
